claims.text: Browser SDK track sends the event object the caller supplies. It does not read data-element or a property contract from the DOM.
claims.where: https://amplitude.com/docs/sdks/analytics/browser/browser-sdk-2/reference (track). Fetched 2026-11-13. Autocapture, on the same page, does read the DOM for clicks and page views. This plugin does not use autocapture to name properties.

claims.text: An enrichment plugin's execute receives the event. If execute does not return the event, the event does not propagate. Returning null drops it.
The generated execute in this plugin always returns an event object, including when the input is missing, and it deletes excluded property names before returning.
claims.where: scripts/amplitude-plugin.test.mjs and the default path of check.mjs. Not run inside the Amplitude SDK.

claims.text: Ampli is a generated client from an Amplitude Data tracking plan. The Browser SDK attaches a plan object (branch, source, version, versionId) to events when configured.

claims.text: Amplitude exposes an is-in-schema flag this plugin should set.
claims.where: Not found on the SDK plugin, Browser SDK reference, or Ampli pages fetched 2026-11-13. This plugin does not invent that flag. A property is in the contract or it is a finding (unknown_property).

claims.text: Amplitude has no DOM access on web.
claims.where: Not established. track does not read the DOM (documented, above). Browser SDK 2 autocapture does. This plugin does not claim the product has no DOM access.

claims.text: Canonical number and integer both become a JSON number on the track payload. A numeric string is refused. date becomes an ISO-8601 string because this plugin does not claim Amplitude has a date type.
claims.where: spec/plugins/amplitude/derive.mjs coerce(), scripts/amplitude-plugin.test.mjs. The mapping is this plugin's rule. It was not sent to Amplitude.

claims.text: An excluded property is refused: trackPayload omits it and records privacy-excluded, and execute deletes it if a caller attached it. The static check exits 1 when a payload still contains it.
There are no hand-authored Amplitude property names. A payload key that is not an identity key and not a contract property is unknown_property.
Element properties and page properties are different scopes. A page-scoped property on a canon:click payload is scope_mismatch.
Native Amplitude SDKs (iOS, Android) consume the same contract.
claims.where: Not written. This plugin derives a web enrichment function and a JSON track payload only.
